title: Chief series and chief factors
source: Keith Conrad, Subgroup Series II, Definition 5.1; D07 composition-series convention as background.
proof_check: Both terms of each factor are normal in the same ambient group; conjugation therefore descends.

title: Existence and the minimal normal criterion
source: Keith Conrad, Subgroup Series II, Theorem 5.3.
proof_check: A maximal chain in a finite normal-subgroup poset is saturated. Quotient correspondence gives the criterion.

title: Equivariant Jordan–Hölder uniqueness for chief factors
source: Robinson, Theorem 3.1.4 (printed p. 66); Milne, Chapter 6 (groups with operators); Keith Conrad, Theorem 5.9.
proof_check: Fix the ambient action while inducting on the endpoint. The two quotient isomorphisms preserve the action and identify the crossed factors.

title: Chief factors of finite solvable groups
source: Keith Conrad, Subgroup Series II, Corollary 5.6; D07 for solvability under subgroups, quotients and extensions.
proof_check: The derived subgroup and, once abelian, the p-torsion subgroup are characteristic. Minimality gives the elementary abelian factor.

title: The two kinds of series in the alternating group
source: Keith Conrad, Subgroup Series II, Examples 5.2 and 5.7; D07 examples of adjacent and ambient normality.
proof_check: Conjugation by a 3-cycle is transitive on the nonidentity elements of V4, and the order-two term is normal in V4 and moved by conjugation in A4.

title: Factor systems for a general kernel
source: Robinson, Section 11.1, Couplings (printed pp. 312–313), for outer actions. Factor-system converse proved here.
proof_check: The conjugation identity and the factor-set identity are both needed for associativity. Section changes preserve the outer homomorphism.

title: Abelian-kernel extensions and H^2
source: Brian Conrad, Group Cohomology and Group Extensions, pp. 1–2; Lassueur, Theorem 24.3.
proof_check: Normalize the cocycle, check that section changes add a coboundary, and construct the inverse extension on A × Q.

title: Complements and H^1
source: Brian Conrad, Group Cohomology and Group Extensions, p. 1; Lassueur, Theorem 23.3.
proof_check: A reference splitting identifies complements with graphs of cocycles. Conjugation by kernel elements adds one-coboundaries.

title: Two extensions of C_2 by C_2
source: Direct normalized-cocycle calculation; related examples in Lassueur, Section 24.
proof_check: The value at (t,t) determines the class. The nonzero value makes the lift of t have order four.

title: The homological five-term sequence
source: Weibel, Theorem 6.8.2 and Low Degree Terms 6.8.3 (printed pp. 195–196); Advanced Homological Algebra, A10.
proof_dependencies: HomAlg:A10 (unnormalized integral bar chains and Tor) | normalized low-degree chains, kernel complex, and transgression computed in this proof
proof_check: The normalization kernel is acyclic through degree two. The chain projection kernel has first homology N/[E,N]; the long exact sequence and the filtered lift give the same signed transgression.

title: Hopf's formula for the Schur multiplier
source: Weibel, Theorem 6.8.8 (printed p. 198); Robinson, Theorem 11.4.15; Lassueur, Theorem 34.7.
proof_check: A free group has a length-one resolution from its Cayley tree. Naturality and the centrality of relators modulo [F,R] show independence of chosen lifts.

title: Multipliers of cyclic groups and their products
source: Direct computation using the Hopf formula.
proof_check: The commutator has order dividing gcd(m,n). Unitriangular matrices attain that order when it exceeds one.

title: Universal central extensions of perfect groups
source: Weibel, Theorem 6.9.5 and preceding lemmas (printed pp. 200–201). Algebraic K-Theory B12 gives a downstream example.
proof_check: Perfectness gives a central-relator product decomposition. Universal lifting uses free generators, and uniqueness follows because the source is perfect.

title: The profinite completion
source: Wilkes, Definition 1.2.1 and Section 1.2; Advanced Field Theory, T04, for the Galois comparison.
proof_check: All finite-index normal subgroups form a cofiltered inverse system, including the trivial quotient.

title: Topology, density, and kernel
source: Wilkes, Remarks 1.2.2–1.2.3 and Proposition 1.2.13; Advanced Field Theory, T06.
proof_check: The closed compatible-tuples subgroup is compact. A single common refinement supplies a representative in each prescribed basic neighborhood.

title: Universal property
source: Wilkes, Section 3.1 and Proposition 3.1.2, comparison with finite targets and functoriality. Arbitrary profinite targets treated by coordinates here.
proof_check: Each finite-coordinate map factors through its kernel. Density proves compatibility and uniqueness.

title: A cofinal family of finite quotients
source: Direct inverse-limit comparison; Wilkes, Section 1.1; Advanced Field Theory, T04, for related inverse-limit conventions.
proof_check: Any two chosen smaller indices have a common refinement, which makes coordinate extension well defined and continuous.

title: The integers and finite fields
source: Wilkes, Section 2.2; Advanced Field Theory, E06, for arithmetic Frobenius.
proof_check: The factorial system is cofinal among the congruence quotients and Frobenius corresponds to the integer 1.

title: Residual finiteness and injectivity
source: Wilkes, Definition 3.1.3 and Proposition 3.1.4.
proof_check: A finite set is separated by intersecting the kernels chosen for its distinct pairs.

title: Finitely generated abelian groups
source: Wilkes, Proposition 3.1.7; D07 finitely generated abelian structure theorem.
proof_check: Projection detects a nonzero finite-summand coordinate. Reduction modulo |a|+1 detects a nonzero integer coordinate a.

title: Free groups
source: Wilkes, Theorem 3.2.1, first proof, and Remark 3.2.2; Geometric Group Theory, A01. Finite permutation construction given here.
proof_check: Reducedness prevents a shared domain or range among the prescribed steps for a generator. The finite permutations move 0 to the word length.

title: The additive rationals
source: Direct calculation using Lagrange’s theorem.
proof_check: Divisibility of the additive rationals makes every homomorphism to a finite group trivial.
